title: Batch geocoding can write failed lookups as real coordinates
reasoning: Failed batch geocodes are cached with latitude and longitude set to 0, then later cache reads include every entry with error_count < 5 without filtering out failures. Because a tuple like (0, 0) is truthy, profiles whose normalized location matches that failed cache entry get latitude=0 and longitude=0 saved as if geocoding succeeded. That corrupts user location data and can make future geocoding skip those profiles because they no longer have null coordinates.
recommendation: Represent failed cache entries with null coordinates or explicitly exclude entries with 0/0 or missing coordinates when building cached_entries, and only save profile coordinates when the cache entry is known successful.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only cover llm_tasks and do not exercise geocoding cache failure paths or batch profile updates.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a batch_geocode_profiles test where geocoder.batch_geocode returns {location: None}; assert the cache records the failure but the matching profile latitude/longitude remain null.
minimumFixScope: Change batch_geocode_profiles cache creation and cached_entries filtering/update logic in hub/tasks/geocoding_tasks.py.
